summary: Seunghak Koh is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Seoul National University and a PhD from UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. in 2011. He was appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Seungsahn Haengwon (1927–2004) was a Buddhist studies figure who attended Dongguk University and studied under traditional teachers including Kobong Sunim, Keumbong, and Geum-o. He succeeded Kobong Sunim in 1957 and founded the Kwan Um School of Zen in 1970.

Seán McLoughlin works in religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Manchester and was a lecturer in South Asian, Islamic, and religious studies at the University of Leeds, attested in 2005.

Shagun Sinha works in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics. He completed doctoral studies supervised by Girish Nath Jha (attested 2022) and was taught by Shashi Prabha Kumar, Ram Nath Jha, and several other instructors.

Shailendra Bhandare is a historian and Indologist who held posts as a British Museum curator and a Fitzwilliam Museum fellow. He served as Assistant Keeper at the Ashmolean Museum (attested 2006–2022) and became a Fellow at St Cross College.

Shaman Hatley is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at Goddard College, he completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (1999–2007), taught at Concordia University (~2007–2015), and became chair of Asian studies at UMass Boston in 2015.

Shan Shan Zhao is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed a Master of Arts degree at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, also studying with Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Shanshan Jia is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. Supervised by Harunaga Isaacson, she pursued doctoral studies at the University of Hamburg (attested 2015, 2026), where she was also a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).

Shaoyong Ye is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies at Peking University in 2009 under Qing Duan. He has served as an associate professor and faculty member at Peking University (attested 2010–2026).
Sharon J. Roe is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2014) under the doctoral supervision of Steven D. Goodman.

Shashibhusan Dasgupta (1911–1964) was an Indian philosopher, Indologist, and religious studies scholar. Educated at Brojomohun College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta (MA, PhD), he lectured at the University of Calcutta from circa 1945 to 1964.

Shayne Clarke is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the University of Canterbury and a PhD at UCLA (2006). He has served as associate professor at McMaster University and research fellow at the IIBS.
Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche (born 1966) is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under spiritual teacher Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and founded the organization Karuna-Shechen in 2000.

Sheila Jasanoff (born 1944) studied at Radcliffe College, the University of Bonn, Harvard University, and Harvard Law School. She held a post at Cornell University (~1978–1998) and became a professor at Harvard Kennedy School around 1998.

Shek-Wing Tam (1935–2024) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. Taught by Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Yingguang Qu, and Yui Chi Lau, he founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies Association in North America and served as a professor at Renmin University.

Sheldon Pollock (born 1948) is an Indologist educated at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held professorships at the University of Iowa, the University of Chicago, and Columbia University, and served as founding editor of the Murty Classical Library.

Sheng Yen (1931–2009) was a Buddhist studies figure who earned doctorates at Rissho University. He founded Dharma Drum Mountain and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and served as a lecturer at Shandao Temple and National Cheng Kung University.

Shenghai Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Supervised by Donald R. Davis Jr., he completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2012) and studied under several teachers, including Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe and Charles Hallisey.

Shenpen Hookham (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied at the University of Reading and completed a D.Phil at the University of Oxford under Michael M. Broido, while also studying under Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.

Shenphen Nangwa (1871–1927) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Mipam Gyatso. He taught at Dzogchen Shri Sengha, became the first khenpo at Dzongsar Monastery, and founded Dzongsar Shedra.
